scopeNote: Six realistic routes to market assessed against publicly observable channel and installation-labour evidence; no partnership, margin, commission or discount is asserted.

channels.name: A — Direct online sales (EMBARCARTE site and checkout)
channels.buyerSegment: Software-first leisure sailor or coastal cruiser who already owns a smartphone/tablet and does not require vessel work; small fleet administrator buying a SaaS tenancy with no hardware.
channels.salesProcess: Self-service: discover, compare editions, purchase an annual entitlement, onboard digitally, self-configure supported inputs, escalate compatibility questions. Hardware compatibility must be an explicit pre-check, never an implied inclusion.
channels.commercialDependency: Own checkout, entitlement/billing platform, payment provider, chart and weather data licences, support staffing. No third party margin is paid, but all acquisition, support, refund and data costs sit on EMBARCARTE.
channels.implementationComplexity: MEDIUM for NAV/WEATHER/FLEET tenancy (software, tax and licensing work); HIGH for anything with hardware, because a D2C hardware order without a compatibility or installation step contradicts the installation model of MC-08 (SFR-1 excluded).
unprovenAssumptions: That Spanish and Portuguese buyers will buy an annual navigation/weather subscription at the portfolio hypothesis price levels; no willingness-to-pay measurement exists.
That chart licensing can be obtained on terms that allow a bundled or inclusive offer; licence rights are BLOCKED under MC-05.
That organic discovery exists at a scale worth serving; SEARCH_INTEREST is INACCESSIBLE and no traffic data was observed.
That a self-service funnel can absorb 'why does my device not connect' support load at an acceptable cost.

economicStructure.observed: Two European specialist online chandleries are estimated at ~USD 13.3M (svb.de, 2025, 0-5% growth) and ~USD 4.9M (compass24.de, 2025, down 20-50%) annual online sales; specialist online nautical retail clearly exists and is volatile.
economicStructure.notPubliclyKnown: Payment fee schedule, refund rate, hosting and data-licence cost, support cost per subscriber, acquisition cost, renewal rate.
economicStructure.marginStatus: UNKNOWN — no cost input is sourced; no margin is claimed.

supportRequirements: Tier-0 self-service: edition matrix, compatibility matrix, supported-device list, offline/degraded-state behaviour.
Tier-1 digital support for account, entitlement, chart region and device connection issues.
Data-protection and cancellation/withdrawal handling; legal review of consumer terms is OPEN.
Export of customer route/log data on cancellation or expiry.
barriers: No approved price exists, so no checkout may be enabled for any SKU.
Chart and weather data licences are BLOCKED, so a sellable NAV/WEATHER scope cannot be published honestly.
MAREA is a proposed brand with brandPublication = NOT_GRANTED; D2C selling would require the clearance and legal seller identity first.
Consumer-law terms (withdrawal, renewal notice, warranty) are OPEN and cannot be improvised at checkout.
channels.validationExperiment: EX-CHN-01: a content-plus-waitlist test on existing site routes measuring (a) qualified 'request a quotation / register interest' submissions by edition, (b) which compatibility questions arrive first, (c) the wording that produces a wrong-price assumption. No page sells or states a price; success threshold fixed in advance by the Lead; instrumenting must remain privacy-reviewed.

channels.name: B — Marine electronics installers (independent and small specialist firms)
channels.buyerSegment: Refit and upgrade customer: owner of a 6-15 m sailing or motor cruiser with mixed-age instruments whose boat needs physical integration, commissioning and handover.
channels.salesProcess: Installer assesses the vessel, proposes a configuration, quotes hardware plus labour separately, installs and commissions, trains the owner, provides first-line support and handles warranty intake.
channels.commercialDependency: Depends entirely on a partner network that does not exist: no agreement, no register, no competence criteria, no rate card (MC-08 §1, §16). The installer's own commercial model depends on labour billing, not on product margin alone.
channels.implementationComplexity: HIGH. Requires a compatibility questionnaire, refusal criteria, installation records, warranty allocation and safety escalation before a single job can be accepted.
unprovenAssumptions: That Iberian installers will adopt a new unproven brand rather than the ecosystems they already install and support.
That measured install time for HUB/AIS on representative vessels is small enough to make the labour line acceptable; no install-hour measurement exists.
That any installer margin is required — and at what level — to compensate their first-line support and warranty exposure.
That the published marina tariff labour rates are a reasonable proxy for independent installer billing; they are a marina's own work-shop rate, not an independent firm's price.

economicStructure.observed: Published marina/yard labour rates in Spain: 59 EUR/h workshop, 76 EUR/h express workshop, 47/65 EUR/h fairing, and an electronics-specific 61 EUR/h at Marina Coruña (2026, VAT excluded); Getxo publishes 32.02 EUR/h; a US marine electrical contractor publishes 180 USD/h standard, 120 USD/h apprentice and 120 USD/h travel with a two-hour minimum.
economicStructure.labourCostBenchmarks: Marine installer gross-salary estimates in ES/PT of 9.49-14 EUR/h; Spanish fully-loaded industrial operator hour 16.70-17.90 EUR; port-tender electrician unit prices 18.11 EUR/h (Oficial 1ª) and 15.69 EUR/h (helper).
economicStructure.notPubliclyKnown: Installer margin on hardware, trade discount, payment terms, stock rotation, labour hours per installation, travel policy, warranty labour reimbursement.
economicStructure.marginStatus: UNKNOWN — no installer margin, discount or commission for MAREA or for any comparable Iberian product was found; only the customer-facing labour rates above are public.

supportRequirements: Technical bulletins, firmware/software release notes and a documented compatibility matrix the installer can trust.
Escalation path to EMBARCARTE engineering for defects and safety-relevant incidents.
Warranty intake process, RMA route and clear allocation of workmanship versus product liability.
Owner-facing training material the installer can deliver, with what is NOT verified stated explicitly.
barriers: No installer network, agreement, register, competence scheme or rate card exists (MC-08 X-05, X-06).
No measured installation time and no validated survey method; PILOT remains gated behind a safety case and sea trials.
A new brand with no installed base creates a support and reputation risk for the installer.
The published labour rates are for yard tasks; a mixed-vessel integration job is quoted per vessel and cannot be inferred from an hourly yard rate.
channels.validationExperiment: EX-CHN-02: structured discovery with 5-8 independent installers in Galicia and Portugal (no MAREA demo, no price list) capturing their current brands, hourly billing, travel policy, typical install hours for a gateway and an AIS receiver, what they charge for first-line support, and what they would require in writing to install an unproven brand. Output: a range of quoted labour hours and billing practices, recorded as DISCOVERY_NOT_PRICE.

channels.name: C — Marine equipment distributors (national wholesalers and pan-European B2B groups)
channels.buyerSegment: Indirect: the distributor's shipchandler and installer account base. The end customer is the same boat owner as channel B, reached through two layers.
channels.salesProcess: Account opening, brand listing, opening order, stocking terms, resale to dealers/installers, logistics and returns through the distributor, with MAREA providing product and technical support.
channels.commercialDependency: Depends on a listing decision by a company whose business is logistics and catalogue breadth, not on marketing a new marine brand. It also depends on MAREA being able to supply at a trade price and honour stock, warranty and returns.
channels.implementationComplexity: HIGH: product data (multilingual catalogue, EAN, manuals, declarations), packaging/logistics, credit and payment terms, stock commitment, after-sales and RMA process, market-price governance.
unprovenAssumptions: That an Iberian wholesaler would list a not-yet-certified brand at all; no approach has been made and no outreach is authorised in MC-09.
That a distributor's required trade discount can be absorbed; no percentage is public, and the anecdote of about 50% of list is US and unverified.
That MAREA can meet listing prerequisites (certification, product data, stock, warranty) inside a first year.
That a distributor would carry the catalogue range rather than a single best-selling SKU.

economicStructure.observed: An Iberian wholesale distribution layer for marine electronics and communications exists (Navegar y Pescar CMC, described as a wholesale distributor for Spain and Portugal). Pan-European groups operate national distribution companies exclusively B2B to shipchandlers, with subsidiaries named in France, Germany, Italy, Spain and Sweden. One US manufacturer publishes a dealer installation-rebate programme; one publishes distributor credit and retention-of-title terms; another operates a dealer-application route.
economicStructure.notPubliclyKnown: Trade discount, volume tiers, payment days, stock rotation, marketing co-op, rebate levels, exclusivity, RMA cost split.
economicStructure.marginStatus: UNKNOWN — no distributor or dealer margin for Spain or Portugal was published in any page reached. The only numeric indication is an unverified US forum anecdote that direct-buying dealers pay about 50% of list.

supportRequirements: Trade product information and training for the distributor's account managers and their dealers.
Spare parts, warranty administration and defined RMA turnaround.
Price-position governance so that published consumer hypotheses are never mistaken for trade or approved prices.
Multilingual manuals and declarations sufficient for catalogue listing.
barriers: No certification or declaration of conformity exists, which is a precondition for catalogue listing.
No approved price or trade-price structure exists, so a distributor conversation would be premature and is out of scope for MC-09.
Two-layer distribution reduces control of the customer relationship and raises support ambiguity.
Distributor listing decisions depend on proven sell-through; MAREA has sold nothing.
channels.validationExperiment: EX-CHN-03 (MC-10 only, subject to Lead authorisation): desk-only mapping of Iberian and pan-European nautical distributors and the listing prerequisites they publish (trade account forms, required product data, certification), with no contact made. Output: a prerequisite checklist and a named list of what must exist before any approach. Success = a documented, non-solicited prerequisite set; no terms are requested or invented.

channels.name: D — Marinas and shipyards (yard services and refit contractors)
channels.buyerSegment: Berth holder undertaking seasonal maintenance or a refit; the marina is both a services provider (labour) and a captive audience with a physical workshop.
channels.salesProcess: Owner books yard time; the yard's own workshop or an external installer performs work; the marina bills infrastructure (crane, ramp, yard days) and labour by task or hour; the sale of electronics may be the yard's own margin line or a referral.
channels.commercialDependency: Depends on yard willingness to install a new brand and on the yard's own service pricing, which is published but heterogeneous. The marina may be a competitor (selling existing brands) rather than a channel.
channels.implementationComplexity: MEDIUM-HIGH: access to vessels, yard scheduling, seasonal peaks, electrical safety responsibility, subcontractor rules, and the fact that each marina prices labour differently.
unprovenAssumptions: That marinas will install third-party-branded electronics rather than products they already distribute.
That yard labour rates observed in Galicia, the Basque Country and Catalonia generalise to Portugal or to the Mediterranean refit yards.
That berth capacity implies electronics install demand; no marina-level installation volume data exists.
That a marina would accept MAREA's limitation and disclaimers as part of its own service liability.

economicStructure.observed: Marinas publish full labour and infrastructure tariffs: Marina Coruña 2026 (59/76/47/65 EUR/h by task, electronics 61 EUR/h, VAT excluded); Getxo 32.02 EUR/h; Ports de la Generalitat crane 60.400 EUR/h and ramp 7.090 EUR/m/day; Marina Palamós 2.50 EUR/m/day yard surcharge for repair works. Spain has 289 recreational ports and 134,200 berths (March 2026).
economicStructure.notPubliclyKnown: Whether marinas buy electronics at trade, what they mark up, how they allocate workshop vs subcontractor work, and how much of the berth base actually installs electronics each year.
economicStructure.marginStatus: UNKNOWN for product margin; the observed public figures are customer-facing labour and infrastructure rates only.

supportRequirements: A clear split between yard workmanship liability and MAREA product liability.
Installation instructions that a general yard workshop, not only a marine-electronics specialist, can follow safely.
Safety escalation for anything touching steering, motor power or tank penetration.
Documented commissioning and handover records.
barriers: No partner agreement, no competence assessment and no insurance position exists.
Marinas already earn on brands they stock; a new brand adds training cost without proven demand.
Yard labour is billed by published tariffs that vary by a factor of more than two across regions, so a single national 'installation price' would be false.
Steering-related work (PILOT) is out of reach until the safety case and conformity work close.
channels.validationExperiment: EX-CHN-04: a tariff and service-catalogue review of 10-15 Spanish and Portuguese marinas/yards, recording published labour rates, whether electronics installation is offered, and what certification or insurance they state. Desk-only, no contact. Output: a regional labour-rate table and a segmentation of yards by stated service scope.

channels.name: E — Charter and fleet operators (rental fleets, sailing schools, fleet managers)
channels.buyerSegment: Multi-vessel professional operator: charter company, sailing school, boat club or manager. Buys a contract, not a product; cares about uptime, staff turnover, insurance evidence and per-vessel cost.
channels.salesProcess: Discovery, pilot on a subset of vessels, written contract (SFR-5), onboarding per vessel, telemetry installation, role/permission setup, support and reporting. Procurement is usually a director/owner decision with a maintenance manager as influencer.
channels.commercialDependency: Depends on a contracted B2B motion and on hardware/connectivity: FLEET's value comes from telemetry, so it depends on HUB/WATCH/SENSE availability, which are BLOCKED. Also depends on data-protection basis for crew and vessel data.
channels.implementationComplexity: HIGH: tenancy isolation, SLAs, onboarding scope, connectivity contracts, per-vessel hardware, multi-user permissions, audit and export.
unprovenAssumptions: That operators will pay a per-vessel monthly fee on top of hardware and connectivity; no Iberian willingness-to-pay evidence exists.
That FLEET can be sold before WATCH/HUB telemetry exists; the dependency is structural, not cosmetic.
That the declining Balearic rental market (about -25% in the 2025 season) leaves budget for software.
That charter operators want software from a new brand rather than the yacht-management suites already marketed to them.

economicStructure.observed: Comparable fleet/yacht SaaS list prices: USD 5.18 per vessel per month in 50-150 vessel blocks with a USD 259 monthly minimum (Rynda); 99-399 EUR plan prices (Scyllastar). Market context: ~3,500 licensed rental boats in the Balearics with day rates 250-15,000 EUR; 1,418 rental registrations nationally in 2025, 321 in the Balearics; 37 marinas and 42 certified nautical stations in Portugal.
economicStructure.notPubliclyKnown: Iberian charter-operator software budgets, procurement cycles, per-vessel connectivity cost, hardware retrofit cost, contract length, churn.
economicStructure.marginStatus: UNKNOWN — SaaS comparators describe price points, not achievable margin; hardware, SIM, onboarding and support costs are unsourced.
economicStructure.channelMarginPercent: UNKNOWN — direct contracted sale assumed; no reseller or agent terms exist.

supportRequirements: Named account support during season, with escalation inside operating hours.
Onboarding per vessel including device registration and consent.
Data-processing terms, retention and deletion, role-based access and audit logs.
A written SLA — none exists (NO_SLA_ESTABLISHED) and none may be promised.
barriers: FLEET Enterprise is NOT_ESTABLISHED; no contracted terms, no tenancy evidence, no onboarding scope.
No hardware telemetry path exists to make FLEET's core promise real.
Data-protection basis for crew/vessel data is OPEN (X-07).
No references, no pilot fleet and no SLA; professional buyers require all three.
channels.validationExperiment: EX-CHN-05: 3-5 discovery interviews with charter/school operators in the Balearics and Galicia about how they currently track vessel status, what they pay for management tools and connectivity, and what evidence they require from a supplier. No product demo, no price quoted, no reference claimed. Output: a problem/priority map and a list of what they would need to see first.

channels.name: F — Nautical e-commerce and specialist retail (multi-brand online stores and chandlers)
channels.buyerSegment: Price-comparing, self-selecting buyer who researches online and either self-installs simple items or buys hardware before hiring an installer.
channels.salesProcess: Catalogue listing, comparison content, cart checkout, shipping; the retailer owns the transaction and the return, MAREA supplies product data and warranty.
channels.commercialDependency: Depends on listing with specialist retailers that already carry Garmin, Raymarine, Simrad, Lowrance and Digital Yacht, on margin structure, and on the retailer's willingness to explain an unproven brand.
channels.implementationComplexity: MEDIUM: catalogue data, logistics, returns, price governance, and the risk that a comparison-driven buyer selects a cheaper incumbents' receiver.
unprovenAssumptions: That an unproven brand can win catalogue space against five or more established electronics brands in the same store.
That online buyers of AIS/gateway hardware will accept an installation requirement disclosed at checkout.
That MAREA's margins survive retail discounting; the only numeric margin indication is an unverified US anecdote.
That traffic exists: no search-volume or traffic-opportunity measurement was obtainable.

economicStructure.observed: Spanish and European specialist online nautical retail exists at catalogue scale (GPS Náutico distributing Garmin, Lowrance, Simrad, Raymarine, Humminbird; MercaNautic self-describing >30,000 products). Third-party estimates: svb.de ~USD 13.3M and compass24.de ~USD 4.9M online sales in 2025. US trade coverage describes manufacturer-set MRP and authorised-dealer policing of discounts.
economicStructure.notPubliclyKnown: Retailer margin, listing fees, returns rate, payment terms, co-op marketing, price-maintenance rules applicable in the EU.
economicStructure.marginStatus: UNKNOWN — no retailer margin or discount was published; the 50%-of-list anecdote is unverified and US-specific.

supportRequirements: Accurate catalogue data, EAN, manuals, and a compatibility statement the retailer can rely on.
Retail return handling and warranty intake.
Content that the retailer can reuse (comparison tables, installation requirements) without misrepresenting certification.
Rapid response to end-customer questions the retailer cannot answer.
barriers: No certification, no BOM, no approved price and no packaging — a catalogue cannot list the product.
Comparison positioning against established brands is unfavourable while prices are unapproved hypotheses.
EU resale-price-maintenance practice must not be modelled on the US MRP description without competition-law review.
Returns of installed marine electronics are commercially and practically different from returns of clothing.
channels.validationExperiment: EX-CHN-06: a structured catalogue audit of 8-12 Spanish, Portuguese and pan-European nautical retailers recording which AIS/gateway/monitoring products they list, how they describe installation, and what information they publish about compatibility. Desk-only. Output: a listing-prerequisite checklist and a competitive shelf map; no contact and no listing request.
